**OPS DATABASE**

**Schema Design & Migration Report**

Four-Way Comparison · All Requested Changes · Migration Roadmap

April 2026

**SCOPE OF THIS REPORT**

This report consolidates the analysis of three source artefacts:

**Ops_db_erd.pdf · Laptop_Data.xlsx · Laptop_Refurbishment_Checklists.docx**

It documents every requested schema change, its location, rationale, and priority,

and provides a full four-way comparison across all schema versions.

# 1\. Executive Summary

The current operational data is stored across 10 Google Sheets tabs. The original ERD documents the intended schema but leaves several structural gaps. A second "New ERD" was proposed adding event-sourcing and QC tables. This report now recommends a fourth, final schema that incorporates all three prior versions plus a relational checklist engine derived from the Refurbishment SOP document.

**Three major categories of work are required:**

- Structural fixes - normalisation of Donor and NGO, primary keys, and FK enforcement.
- Data quality remediation - enumeration of free-text fields that have drifted in the live sheet data.
- New capability - a fully relational checklist engine covering all 6 lifecycle stages, stage gate enforcement, issue severity tracking, and monthly monitoring.

The recommended schema grows from 10 tables to 22, adds approximately 145 checklist items across 6 stages, and for the first time makes stage-gate rules enforceable in software rather than just documented in a Word file.

# 2\. All Requested Changes

Each row below represents a discrete change request. Priority is: Critical = data integrity risk, High = operational gap, Medium = improvement.

| **#** | **Change Type**   | **Priority** | **Where**                                                     | **What & Why**                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----- | ----------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1     | **Normalization** | **Critical** | LAPTOP_LABELING, PICKUP, PRELIMINARY, EXTERNAL_REGISTERED_NGO | Create a DONOR table. "donor_company_name", "donor_company", and "Doner" are 3 different spellings of the same FK across 4 tables. Single source of truth eliminates drift and enables reporting by donor.         |
| 2     | **Normalization** | **Critical** | USER_DETAILS (ngo col), PRELIMINARY (ngoId), REPORT (ngoId)   | Create an NGO table. NGO is stored as free text in UserDetails and as an unvalidated ID string in Preliminary/Report. Formal table with FK enforces referential integrity and enables NGO-level dashboards.        |
| 3     | **Data Quality**  | **Critical** | LAPTOP_LABELING - condition_status column                     | Enum-ify condition_status. Live data contains 10 variants of 3 intended values (GOOD, BAD, NEEDS REPAIR) due to mixed case and whitespace. Add a CHECK constraint or application-level enum before migration.      |
| 4     | **Data Quality**  | **Critical** | LAPTOP_LABELING - working column                              | Merge "working" into "status". Status has 5 lifecycle values; working has "Working / Not Working" - they overlap and cause drift. One status field with a clean enum covers both.                                  |
| 5     | **Schema Fix**    | **Critical** | LAPTOP_USER_MAP sheet / table                                 | Add map_id primary key and enforce UNIQUE(laptop_id, user_id). The sheet has no PK and only 8 rows - likely under-populated due to the missing constraint allowing silent duplicates.                              |
| 6     | **Schema Fix**    | **High**     | LAPTOP_LABELING - allocated_to and assigned_to columns        | Split into two typed FKs: allocated_ngo_id (FK → NGO) and assigned_user_id (FK → USER_DETAILS). Currently both are free-text with different semantic meaning - allocated_to is an org, assigned_to is a person.    |
| 7     | **New Table**     | **High**     | Between PICKUP and LAPTOP_LABELING                            | Add PICKUP_LAPTOP_MAP junction table. PICKUP.number_of_laptops stores only a count; there is no way to trace which specific laptop IDs came from which pickup event. Critical for donor accountability.            |
| 8     | **New Table**     | **High**     | New - replaces status text field                              | Add STAGE_DEFINITION table with 6 rows (one per lifecycle stage), capturing stage_name, sla_hours, responsible_role, verifier_role, and requires_different_actor flag.                                             |
| 9     | **New Table**     | **High**     | New - per laptop per stage                                    | Add LAPTOP_STAGE_RUN. Tracks each attempt to complete a stage for a specific laptop, with started_by, completed_by, verifier_name, outcome, and timestamps. Enables SLA breach calculation per stage.              |
| 10    | **New Table**     | **High**     | New - relational checklist engine                             | Add CHECKLIST_SECTION and CHECKLIST_ITEM tables. All ~145 checklist items from the SOP document become rows, grouped by section within each stage. Items can be updated without schema changes.                    |
| 11    | **New Table**     | **High**     | New - per checklist item per run                              | Add CHECKLIST_RESPONSE. Records pass/fail/remark and evidence_url per item per stage run. Replaces the current practice of storing condition as a single free-text field.                                          |
| 12    | **New Table**     | **High**     | New - stage gate enforcement                                  | Add STAGE_GATE_RULE and STAGE_GATE_EVALUATION. Each blocking condition from the SOP ("device cannot proceed if…") becomes a row. Pass/fail is recorded and queryable, not just checked manually.                   |
| 13    | **New Table**     | **High**     | New - post-dispatch monitoring                                | Add MONTHLY_CHECK_IN. Models Stage 5 (15-day follow-up) and Stage 6 (monthly monitoring) which are entirely absent from all prior schemas. Captures RMS status, active users, use case, impact notes per check-in. |
| 14    | **New Table**     | **High**     | New - replaces ISSUE_FEEDBACK                                 | Add ISSUE_LOG with P1/P2/P3 severity, source stage run FK, resolution_action, resolved_at, and status. The existing "Not Working" terminal status captures no cause, severity, or resolution detail.               |
| 15    | **Inherited**     | **High**     | From New ERD - LAPTOP_EVENT_LOG                               | Retain append-only field-level event log. The 128,000-row audit sheet confirms the volume is real. This table is the write-side of the event sourcing pattern.                                                     |
| 16    | **Inherited**     | **High**     | From New ERD - LAPTOP_VERSIONS                                | Retain full JSON snapshots per change. The audit sheet captures diffs but cannot reconstruct the laptop state at a point in time. LAPTOP_VERSIONS fills this gap.                                                  |
| 17    | **Schema Fix**    | **Medium**   | ACTIVITY sheet / table                                        | Add laptop_id FK to ACTIVITY table (serial column is implicitly the laptop ID). The sheet is currently empty but the schema lacks a FK, making it impossible to query activity by laptop.                          |
| 18    | **Data Quality**  | **Medium**   | METRICS_BASE - col_3, col_4 columns                           | Rename placeholder columns and add a field_type column (material_weight, carbon, toxic, impact_metric). The multiplier-based impact calculations need typed inputs to be dashboard-safe.                           |
| 19    | **Schema Fix**    | **Medium**   | AVERAGE_DAYS_COUNT sheet / table                              | The sheet is empty. With LAPTOP_STAGE_RUN providing started_at and completed_at per stage, this table can be computed as a view rather than maintained manually.                                                   |
| 20    | **Data Quality**  | **Medium**   | PRELIMINARY - Unit column                                     | Column contains timestamps rather than unit values in live data. Clarify intended data type and clean before migration.                                                                                            |

Replaces free-text donor fields scattered across 4 tables.   |

| **STAGE_DEFINITION**      | **Core lifecycle**   | stage_id PK, stage_number, stage_name, sla_hours, responsible_role, verifier_role, requires_different_actor                                                                           | Master table for the 6 lifecycle stages. Source for SLA breach reporting.                           |

Updatable without schema change.            |

Replaces the "Not Working" terminal status and ISSUE_FEEDBACK. |

First time this data has a schema home.                |

# 5\. Checklist Stages - Items & Gates

Derived from Laptop_Refurbishment_Checklists_Detailed.docx. All items become rows in CHECKLIST_ITEM. All gate rules become rows in STAGE_GATE_RULE.

| **Stage**                            | **Checklist Sections**                                                                                                | **Items (approx)** | **Gate Blockers**         | **SLA**                         |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| **Stage 1 Laptop Received**          | Serial verification · Dashboard upload · Physical condition assessment · Tagging                                      | **~18 items**      | **4 blockers**            | 24-48 hours of physical receipt |
| **Stage 2 Refurbishment & Testing**  | Hardware cleaning · Storage wipe · Functional testing (Power, Input, Battery, Ports, Camera/Audio) · Software setup   | **~45 items**      | **5 blockers**            | 2-3 weeks from intake           |
| **Stage 3 QC Check**                 | Re-verification of Stage 2 · Performance test · OS & software verify · Final security configuration                   | **~30 items**      | **6 blockers**            | 48 hours before dispatch date   |
| **Stage 4 Distribution**             | Pre-dispatch verification · Packaging · Dashboard & documentation · NGO partner notification                          | **~16 items**      | **3 blockers**            | 48 hours post QC approval       |
| **Stage 5 Post-Deployment (15-day)** | NGO partner contact · Issue identification & logging · RMS verification · Satisfaction & impact check                 | **~14 items**      | **2 triggers**            | Within 15 days of dispatch      |
| **Stage 6 Monthly Monitoring**       | Monthly partner check-in · Usage & impact tracking · Technical health review · Issue management · End-of-life (12mo+) | **~22 items**      | **5 escalation triggers** | First 10 days of each month     |

### Stage gate rules by stage

The following blocking conditions from the SOP document are proposed as rows in STAGE_GATE_RULE (blocks_progression = true):

### Stage 1 gate rules

- Any dashboard field left blank or marked unknown.
- Photographs not uploaded.
- Serial number could not be verified.
- Barcode not physically affixed and scanned.

### Stage 2 gate rules

- Any functional test not completed.
- Any test result recorded as FAIL without approved resolution.
- RMS not installed and confirmed active.
- Dashboard not updated with all test results.
- Device status remains Repair Required with unresolved issues.

### Stage 3 gate rules

- QC performed by the same person who completed Stage 2 (requires_different_actor enforced).
- Any QC check item incomplete or unresolved.
- Windows not activated.
- BIOS password not set.
- RMS not confirmed active.
- QC outcome not recorded with approver name and date.

### Stage 4 gate rules

- Device status in dashboard is not QC Approved.
- Any required dispatch field incomplete.
- No acknowledgement or tracking confirmation obtained.

# 6\. Data Quality Issues Found in Live Sheet Data

These issues were identified by reading the actual Laptop_Data.xlsx content (14,984 rows in Laptop Labeling, 128,416 rows in Audit). They must be remediated before or during migration to the database.

| **Field / Table**                        | **Issue Found in Sheets**                                                                                                                                                              | **Impact**                                                                                                                               | **Recommended Fix**                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **condition_status (LAPTOP_LABELING)**   | 10 variants of 3 intended values: "GOOD", "BAD", "Needs Repair", "needs repair", "NEEDS REPAIR", "NEEDS REPAIR: Camera not found", "Needs Repair ", "need repair", "GOOD ", plus nulls | Any WHERE condition_status = 'GOOD' misses rows. Dashboard filters will show 7 phantom categories. Aggregations are wrong.               | Normalise to enum {GOOD, BAD, NEEDS_REPAIR} with a migration script before import. Add CHECK constraint in DB.                                |
| **working (LAPTOP_LABELING)**            | 3 values: "Working", "Not Working", null - overlaps semantically with the status field which has 5 lifecycle values                                                                    | A device can be status=Distributed and working=Not Working simultaneously with no resolution path. Confusion in reporting.               | Merge working into status enum. Remove the working column. Status values: RECEIVED, REFURBISHMENT_STARTED, REFURBISHED, DISTRIBUTED, RETIRED. |
| **allocated_to (LAPTOP_LABELING)**       | Contains NGO organisation names as free text (e.g. "Peepul", "LEARNING LINKS FOUNDATION") - 10+ distinct values seen                                                                   | No FK to NGO table. Spelling variants will create phantom NGOs in reports. Cannot join to PRELIMINARY or REPORT.                         | After creating NGO table, run a lookup migration to replace text with ngo_id FK. Flag unmatched rows for manual review.                       |
| **assigned_to (LAPTOP_LABELING)**        | Contains individual person names as free text - semantically different from allocated_to but same column type                                                                          | Cannot query "all laptops assigned to a specific person" reliably. No link to USER_DETAILS.                                              | Rename to assigned_user_name (text, nullable) or add assigned_user_id FK to USER_DETAILS where the user exists.                               |
| **donor_company_name (LAPTOP_LABELING)** | "doner" typo in original ERD. Live data has company names as free text. PICKUP has "donor_company". PRELIMINARY has "Doner".                                                           | Three disconnected donor references. Donor-level reporting (total devices, pickups, impact) is impossible without manual reconciliation. | Create DONOR table. Run match-and-map migration across all three columns. Enforce FK post-migration.                                          |
| **Unit column (PRELIMINARY)**            | Column contains timestamp values in live data (e.g. "2025-01-22 15:04:44") rather than unit/course identifiers                                                                         | Column is semantically broken. Cannot be used for any analytical query.                                                                  | Clarify intended meaning with stakeholders. If it is a date, rename to submission_date. Otherwise fix at source before migration.             |
| **LaptopUserMap (sheet)**                | No primary key column. Only 8 rows total despite 980 users and 14,984 laptops - almost certainly under-populated.                                                                      | Duplicate assignments cannot be detected. The mapping between users and laptops is effectively lost.                                     | Add map_id PK (serial). Add UNIQUE(laptop_id, user_id). Audit and backfill from audit log where possible.                                     |
| **PICKUP.number_of_laptops (integer)**   | Only a count - no link to individual laptop IDs. 3 pickup records with 15 laptops each but no detail.                                                                                  | Cannot tell which laptops came from which pickup. Donor accountability and batch traceability are broken.                                | Add PICKUP_LAPTOP_MAP junction table (pickup_id FK, laptop_id FK). Backfill from audit log using pickup dates.                                |
| **METRICS_BASE (col_3, col_4)**          | Generic column names. Table is used for impact metric multipliers (carbon, toxic waste) but field types are undefined.                                                                 | No type safety. Dashboard can show a "Trainers Enabled" value of "based on user status change" - unparseable.                            | Rename col_3 → unit, col_4 → notes. Add field_type enum (material_weight, carbon_factor, toxic_factor, impact_metric).                        |

# 7\. Recommended Migration Roadmap

Sequenced in dependency order. Each phase can be deployed independently.

### Phase 1 - Foundation (Critical, do first)

- Create DONOR table. Run match-and-map across LAPTOP_LABELING, PICKUP, PRELIMINARY.
- Create NGO table. FK from USER_DETAILS, PRELIMINARY, REPORT.
- Normalise condition_status to enum. Run migration script on all 14,984 rows.
- Merge working column into status. Update status enum values.
- Add map_id PK and UNIQUE constraint to LAPTOP_USER_MAP.

### Phase 2 - Lifecycle Control (High)

- Create STAGE_DEFINITION with 6 rows. Populate SLA hours and roles.
- Create LAPTOP_STAGE_RUN. Migrate current status values to first stage run records.
- Create STAGE_GATE_RULE. Populate from SOP document (18 blocking rules across 4 stages).
- Create PICKUP_LAPTOP_MAP. Backfill from audit log using pickup dates where possible.
- Inherit LAPTOP_EVENT_LOG and LAPTOP_VERSIONS from New ERD. Migrate audit sheet data.

### Phase 3 - Checklist Engine (High)

- Create CHECKLIST_SECTION and CHECKLIST_ITEM. Seed with ~145 items from the SOP document.
- Create CHECKLIST_RESPONSE. Wire to LAPTOP_STAGE_RUN and CHECKLIST_ITEM.
- Create STAGE_GATE_EVALUATION. Wire to STAGE_GATE_RULE and LAPTOP_STAGE_RUN.
- Implement requires_different_actor validation in application layer or DB trigger.

### Phase 4 - Monitoring & Impact (High / Medium)

- Create ISSUE_LOG. Migrate existing "Not Working" records with severity defaulting to P2.
- Create MONTHLY_CHECK_IN. Begin populating from first check-in cycle post-launch.
- Replace AVERAGE_DAYS_COUNT manual table with a computed view over LAPTOP_STAGE_RUN.
- Rename METRICS_BASE columns and add field_type enum.

"donor_company_name", "donor_company", and "Doner" are 3 different spellings of the same FK across 4 tables. Single source of truth eliminates drift and enables reporting by donor. |
| 2 | Normalization | Critical | USER_DETAILS (ngo col), PRELIMINARY (ngoId), REPORT (ngoId) | Create an NGO table. NGO is stored as free text in UserDetails and as an unvalidated ID string in Preliminary/Report. Formal table with FK enforces referential integrity and enables NGO-level dashboards. |
| 3 | Data Quality | Critical | LAPTOP_LABELING — condition_status column | Enum-ify condition_status. Live data contains 10 variants of 3 intended values (GOOD, BAD, NEEDS REPAIR) due to mixed case and whitespace. Add a CHECK constraint or application-level enum before migration. |
| 4 | Data Quality | Critical | LAPTOP_LABELING — working column | Merge "working" into "status". Status has 5 lifecycle values; working has "Working / Not Working" — they overlap and cause drift. One status field with a clean enum covers both. |
| 5 | Schema Fix | Critical | LAPTOP_USER_MAP sheet / table | Add map_id primary key and enforce UNIQUE(laptop_id, user_id). The sheet has no PK and only 8 rows — likely under-populated due to the missing constraint allowing silent duplicates. |
| 6 | Schema Fix | High | LAPTOP_LABELING — allocated_to and assigned_to columns | Split into two typed FKs: allocated_ngo_id (FK → NGO) and assigned_user_id (FK → USER_DETAILS). Currently both are free-text with different semantic meaning — allocated_to is an org, assigned_to is a person. |
| 7 | New Table | High | Between PICKUP and LAPTOP_LABELING | Add PICKUP_LAPTOP_MAP junction table. PICKUP.number_of_laptops stores only a count; there is no way to trace which specific laptop IDs came from which pickup event. Critical for donor accountability. |
| 8 | New Table | High | New — replaces status text field | Add STAGE_DEFINITION table with 6 rows (one per lifecycle stage), capturing stage_name, sla_hours, responsible_role, verifier_role, and requires_different_actor flag. |
| 9 | New Table | High | New — per laptop per stage | Add LAPTOP_STAGE_RUN. Tracks each attempt to complete a stage for a specific laptop, with started_by, completed_by, verifier_name, outcome, and timestamps. Enables SLA breach calculation per stage. |
| 10 | New Table | High | New — relational checklist engine | Add CHECKLIST_SECTION and CHECKLIST_ITEM tables. All ~145 checklist items from the SOP document become rows, grouped by section within each stage. Items can be updated without schema changes. |
| 11 | New Table | High | New — per checklist item per run | Add CHECKLIST_RESPONSE. Records pass/fail/remark and evidence_url per item per stage run. Replaces the current practice of storing condition as a single free-text field. |
| 12 | New Table | High | New — stage gate enforcement | Add STAGE_GATE_RULE and STAGE_GATE_EVALUATION. Each blocking condition from the SOP ("device cannot proceed if…") becomes a row. Pass/fail is recorded and queryable, not just checked manually. |
| 13 | New Table | High | New — post-dispatch monitoring | Add MONTHLY_CHECK_IN. Models Stage 5 (15-day follow-up) and Stage 6 (monthly monitoring) which are entirely absent from all prior schemas. Captures RMS status, active users, use case, impact notes per check-in. |
| 14 | New Table | High | New — replaces ISSUE_FEEDBACK | Add ISSUE_LOG with P1/P2/P3 severity, source stage run FK, resolution_action, resolved_at, and status. The existing "Not Working" terminal status captures no cause, severity, or resolution detail. |
| 15 | Inherited | High | From New ERD — LAPTOP_EVENT_LOG | Retain append-only field-level event log. The 128,000-row audit sheet confirms the volume is real. This table is the write-side of the event sourcing pattern. |
| 16 | Inherited | High | From New ERD — LAPTOP_VERSIONS | Retain full JSON snapshots per change. The audit sheet captures diffs but cannot reconstruct the laptop state at a point in time. LAPTOP_VERSIONS fills this gap. |
| 17 | Schema Fix | Medium | ACTIVITY sheet / table | Add laptop_id FK to ACTIVITY table (serial column is implicitly the laptop ID). The sheet is currently empty but the schema lacks a FK, making it impossible to query activity by laptop. |
| 18 | Data Quality | Medium | METRICS_BASE — col_3, col_4 columns | Rename placeholder columns and add a field_type column (material_weight, carbon, toxic, impact_metric). The multiplier-based impact calculations need typed inputs to be dashboard-safe. |
| 19 | Schema Fix | Medium | AVERAGE_DAYS_COUNT sheet / table | The sheet is empty. With LAPTOP_STAGE_RUN providing started_at and completed_at per stage, this table can be computed as a view rather than maintained manually. |
| 20 | Data Quality | Medium | PRELIMINARY — Unit column | Column contains timestamps rather than unit values in live data. Clarify intended data type and clean before migration. |

# 4\. New Tables in the Recommended Schema

All 12 new tables relative to the original ERD, grouped by purpose.

| Table Name | Category | Key Fields | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DONOR | Core lifecycle | id PK, company_name, poc_name, poc_contact, poc_email | Single source of truth for all donor organisations. Replaces free-text donor fields scattered across 4 tables. |
| NGO | Core lifecycle | id PK, name, donor_id FK, state, contact_email | Normalises NGO identity. FK from UserDetails, Preliminary, and Report. |
| PICKUP_LAPTOP_MAP | Core lifecycle | map_id PK, pickup_id FK, laptop_id FK | Junction table linking each pickup event to the specific laptops collected. Enables donor-level traceability. |
| STAGE_DEFINITION | Core lifecycle | stage_id PK, stage_number, stage_name, sla_hours, responsible_role, verifier_role, requires_different_actor | Master table for the 6 lifecycle stages. SLA and role data stored here, not hardcoded. |
| LAPTOP_STAGE_RUN | Core lifecycle | run_id PK, laptop_id FK, stage_id FK, run_status, started_by, started_at, completed_by, completed_at, verifier_name, outcome | Tracks each attempt to complete a stage for a device. Source for SLA breach reporting. |
| STAGE_GATE_RULE | Core lifecycle | rule_id PK, stage_id FK, rule_description, blocks_progression | Each "device cannot proceed if…" condition from the SOP as a data row. Makes gates queryable. |
| STAGE_GATE_EVALUATION | Core lifecycle | eval_id PK, run_id FK, rule_id FK, passed, failure_note, evaluated_at, evaluated_by | Records pass/fail of every gate rule per stage run. Enables gate audit trail. |
| CHECKLIST_SECTION | Checklist engine | section_id PK, stage_id FK, section_name, display_order | Groups checklist items within a stage (e.g. "Hardware Cleaning", "Functional Testing"). |
| CHECKLIST_ITEM | Checklist engine | item_id PK, section_id FK, item_text, item_type, display_order, is_blocking | One row per checklist line from the SOP. ~145 items across 6 stages. Updatable without schema change. |
| CHECKLIST_RESPONSE | Checklist engine | response_id PK, run_id FK, item_id FK, response_value, responded_by, responded_at, remark, evidence_url | Technician responses per item per stage run. evidence_url supports photo and document uploads per item. |
| ISSUE_LOG | Monitoring | issue_id PK, laptop_id FK, run_id FK, issue_description, severity, reported_by, reported_at, resolution_action, resolved_at, status | Structured issue tracking with P1/P2/P3 severity. Replaces the "Not Working" terminal status and ISSUE_FEEDBACK. |
| MONTHLY_CHECK_IN | Monitoring | checkin_id PK, laptop_id FK, checkin_date, ngo_contact_person, device_status, active_users_count, primary_use_case, rms_status, rms_last_seen, impact_notes, action_items, updated_by | Models Stage 5 (15-day) and Stage 6 (monthly) monitoring. First time this data has a schema home. |

# 5\. Checklist Stages — Items & Gates

Derived from Laptop\_Refurbishment\_Checklists\_Detailed.docx. All items become rows in CHECKLIST\_ITEM. All gate rules become rows in STAGE\_GATE\_RULE.

| Stage | Checklist Sections | Items (approx) | Gate Blockers | SLA |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stage 1 Laptop Received | Serial verification · Dashboard upload · Physical condition assessment · Tagging | ~18 items | 4 blockers | 24–48 hours of physical receipt |
| Stage 2 Refurbishment & Testing | Hardware cleaning · Storage wipe · Functional testing (Power, Input, Battery, Ports, Camera/Audio) · Software setup | ~45 items | 5 blockers | 2–3 weeks from intake |
| Stage 3 QC Check | Re-verification of Stage 2 · Performance test · OS & software verify · Final security configuration | ~30 items | 6 blockers | 48 hours before dispatch date |
| Stage 4 Distribution | Pre-dispatch verification · Packaging · Dashboard & documentation · NGO partner notification | ~16 items | 3 blockers | 48 hours post QC approval |
| Stage 5 Post-Deployment (15-day) | NGO partner contact · Issue identification & logging · RMS verification · Satisfaction & impact check | ~14 items | 2 triggers | Within 15 days of dispatch |
| Stage 6 Monthly Monitoring | Monthly partner check-in · Usage & impact tracking · Technical health review · Issue management · End-of-life (12mo+) | ~22 items | 5 escalation triggers | First 10 days of each month |

### Stage gate rules by stage

The following blocking conditions from the SOP document are proposed as rows in STAGE\_GATE\_RULE (blocks\_progression = true):

### Stage 1 gate rules

*   Any dashboard field left blank or marked unknown.
*   Photographs not uploaded.
*   Serial number could not be verified.
*   Barcode not physically affixed and scanned.

### Stage 2 gate rules

*   Any functional test not completed.
*   Any test result recorded as FAIL without approved resolution.
*   RMS not installed and confirmed active.
*   Dashboard not updated with all test results.
*   Device status remains Repair Required with unresolved issues.

### Stage 3 gate rules

*   QC performed by the same person who completed Stage 2 (requires\_different\_actor enforced).
*   Any QC check item incomplete or unresolved.
*   Windows not activated.
*   BIOS password not set.
*   RMS not confirmed active.
*   QC outcome not recorded with approver name and date.

### Stage 4 gate rules

*   Device status in dashboard is not QC Approved.
*   Any required dispatch field incomplete.
*   No acknowledgement or tracking confirmation obtained.

# 6\. Data Quality Issues Found in Live Sheet Data

These issues were identified by reading the actual Laptop\_Data.xlsx content (14,984 rows in Laptop Labeling, 128,416 rows in Audit). They must be remediated before or during migration to the database.

| Field / Table | Issue Found in Sheets | Impact | Recommended Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| condition_status (LAPTOP_LABELING) | 10 variants of 3 intended values: "GOOD", "BAD", "Needs Repair", "needs repair", "NEEDS REPAIR", "NEEDS REPAIR: Camera not found", "Needs Repair ", "need repair", "GOOD ", plus nulls | Any WHERE condition_status = 'GOOD' misses rows. Dashboard filters will show 7 phantom categories. Aggregations are wrong. | Normalise to enum {GOOD, BAD, NEEDS_REPAIR} with a migration script before import. Add CHECK constraint in DB. |
| working (LAPTOP_LABELING) | 3 values: "Working", "Not Working", null — overlaps semantically with the status field which has 5 lifecycle values | A device can be status=Distributed and working=Not Working simultaneously with no resolution path. Confusion in reporting. | Merge working into status enum. Remove the working column. Status values: RECEIVED, REFURBISHMENT_STARTED, REFURBISHED, DISTRIBUTED, RETIRED. |
| allocated_to (LAPTOP_LABELING) | Contains NGO organisation names as free text (e.g. "Peepul", "LEARNING LINKS FOUNDATION") — 10+ distinct values seen | No FK to NGO table. Spelling variants will create phantom NGOs in reports. Cannot join to PRELIMINARY or REPORT. | After creating NGO table, run a lookup migration to replace text with ngo_id FK. Flag unmatched rows for manual review. |
| assigned_to (LAPTOP_LABELING) | Contains individual person names as free text — semantically different from allocated_to but same column type | Cannot query "all laptops assigned to a specific person" reliably. No link to USER_DETAILS. | Rename to assigned_user_name (text, nullable) or add assigned_user_id FK to USER_DETAILS where the user exists. |
| donor_company_name (LAPTOP_LABELING) | "doner" typo in original ERD. Live data has company names as free text. PICKUP has "donor_company". PRELIMINARY has "Doner". | Three disconnected donor references. Donor-level reporting (total devices, pickups, impact) is impossible without manual reconciliation. | Create DONOR table. Run match-and-map migration across all three columns. Enforce FK post-migration. |
| Unit column (PRELIMINARY) | Column contains timestamp values in live data (e.g. "2025-01-22 15:04:44") rather than unit/course identifiers | Column is semantically broken. Cannot be used for any analytical query. | Clarify intended meaning with stakeholders. If it is a date, rename to submission_date. Otherwise fix at source before migration. |
| LaptopUserMap (sheet) | No primary key column. Only 8 rows total despite 980 users and 14,984 laptops — almost certainly under-populated. | Duplicate assignments cannot be detected. The mapping between users and laptops is effectively lost. | Add map_id PK (serial). Add UNIQUE(laptop_id, user_id). Audit and backfill from audit log where possible. |
| PICKUP.number_of_laptops (integer) | Only a count — no link to individual laptop IDs. 3 pickup records with 15 laptops each but no detail. | Cannot tell which laptops came from which pickup. Donor accountability and batch traceability are broken. | Add PICKUP_LAPTOP_MAP junction table (pickup_id FK, laptop_id FK). Backfill from audit log using pickup dates. |
| METRICS_BASE (col_3, col_4) | Generic column names. Table is used for impact metric multipliers (carbon, toxic waste) but field types are undefined. | No type safety. Dashboard can show a "Trainers Enabled" value of "based on user status change" — unparseable. | Rename col_3 → unit, col_4 → notes. Add field_type enum (material_weight, carbon_factor, toxic_factor, impact_metric). |

# 7\. Recommended Migration Roadmap

Sequenced in dependency order. Each phase can be deployed independently.

### Phase 1 — Foundation (Critical, do first)

1.  Create DONOR table. Run match-and-map across LAPTOP\_LABELING, PICKUP, PRELIMINARY.
2.  Create NGO table. FK from USER\_DETAILS, PRELIMINARY, REPORT.
3.  Normalise condition\_status to enum. Run migration script on all 14,984 rows.
4.  Merge working column into status. Update status enum values.
5.  Add map\_id PK and UNIQUE constraint to LAPTOP\_USER\_MAP.

### Phase 2 — Lifecycle Control (High)

1.  Create STAGE\_DEFINITION with 6 rows. Populate SLA hours and roles.
2.  Create LAPTOP\_STAGE\_RUN. Migrate current status values to first stage run records.
3.  Create STAGE\_GATE\_RULE. Populate from SOP document (18 blocking rules across 4 stages).
4.  Create PICKUP\_LAPTOP\_MAP. Backfill from audit log using pickup dates where possible.
5.  Inherit LAPTOP\_EVENT\_LOG and LAPTOP\_VERSIONS from New ERD. Migrate audit sheet data.

### Phase 3 — Checklist Engine (High)

1.  Create CHECKLIST\_SECTION and CHECKLIST\_ITEM. Seed with ~145 items from the SOP document.
2.  Create CHECKLIST\_RESPONSE. Wire to LAPTOP\_STAGE\_RUN and CHECKLIST\_ITEM.
3.  Create STAGE\_GATE\_EVALUATION. Wire to STAGE\_GATE\_RULE and LAPTOP\_STAGE\_RUN.
4.  Implement requires\_different\_actor validation in application layer or DB trigger.

### Phase 4 — Monitoring & Impact (High / Medium)

1.  Create ISSUE\_LOG. Migrate existing "Not Working" records with severity defaulting to P2.
2.  Create MONTHLY\_CHECK\_IN. Begin populating from first check-in cycle post-launch.
3.  Replace AVERAGE\_DAYS\_COUNT manual table with a computed view over LAPTOP\_STAGE\_RUN.
4.  Rename METRICS\_BASE columns and add field\_type enum.

End of Report — Ops DB Schema Design & Migration Analysis
